title: Syllabus
description: YAML front matter of course/syllabus/syllabus.md — the course-level top layer (D-021, D-043). Front matter holds what tools or agents USE: the goal, Course Outcomes, the unit map, workload, prerequisites, reading, grading, and the teacher's approval. What only people read — the catalogue description, teaching methods, level, policies, an AI-use policy — is body sections, in the institution's own order. Identity fields (title, code, textbooks) are NOT repeated here; they live in course.yaml. Best effort, not a form: only `goal` and `outcomes` are required.

accepted.description: The teacher's deliberate exceptions for THIS file (D-037). Each entry suppresses one validation rule's findings for this file; `classkit validate` still counts them, so they are never invisible. Only the teacher adds these — an agent never does so on its own.

rule.description: The rule code, as `classkit validate` prints it in brackets, e.g. 'in_class_missing'. Not pattern-checked on purpose: a mistyped code is reported by the advisory rule `unknown_rule`, never as a schema error (D-038).

id.description: Optional (D-048): the one item this exception covers — an objective (U01-O3), a guiding question (U01-S02-G1), an activity (U01-A1), an assessment item (U01-I01), a unit (U03) or a material locator (M0007#slide-3). Without it, the exception covers the rule's findings for the whole file. An id that matches nothing is counted with the stale entries.

reason.description: Why the departure is deliberate, e.g. 'holiday week — no class meeting'. Optional: a missing reason is reported by the advisory rule `accepted_without_reason`, never as a schema error (D-038).

outcomes.description: Course Outcomes — the roof of the coverage chain (D-021). Every Unit Objective rolls up to at least one of these, and every one of these is covered by at least one Unit Objective, so 'do the units together deliver what the course promised?' is checkable at course scope.

statement.description: What a student who passes the course can do. An outcome, not a subject label.

unit_map.description: The whole semester's plan, written before most units exist (D-040, D-043): which units the course has, in what order, with what titles. Authoritative for that; a units/NN-slug/ directory is created only when a unit is planned in detail (/plan-units).

number.description: The unit's number — its week in the semester's order.

summary.description: A line on what the unit covers.

evidence.description: Material locators the plan for this unit rests on, e.g. 'M0007#slide-1', 'M0003#page-12'. What a later agent reads first when it plans the unit.

workload.description: Optional (D-031d): a teacher may draft and validate a syllabus before credits are settled. While it is absent, `syllabus_workload_missing` warns. Note that no credit system is hardcoded — ECTS is one instantiation of `credit_system`, not the framework's assumption (invariant 2).

credit_system.description: The system the credits are counted in, e.g. 'ECTS', 'BGU points', 'US semester hours'.

total_hours.description: Total student hours the course is meant to cost, contact and independent study together.

prerequisites.description: Course-level prerequisites: free text, or the codes of other courses. Unit-level prerequisites live on the unit.

reading.description: The course's reading list (D-032). Each entry is a `textbooks[].key` from course.yaml (preferred — no duplication), or free text for anything not listed there.

assessment.description: The grading scheme, e.g. [{type: exam, weight: 60}, {type: homework, weight: 40}]. The syllabus-designer may draft it — from an old syllabus, or by asking the teacher, never invented (D-043); nothing validates its content, and approving or editing it is the teacher's responsibility. Its item shape is deliberately left open (no additionalProperties: false): the Assessment phase will give grading real structure, and may then ask for what was written freely to be converted.

description.description: What the component is, in a line — e.g. 'six problem sets; the lowest is dropped'.

approved.description: The teacher's approval of this syllabus — the milestone unit work builds on (D-043, spec §8.9). Written by `classkit approve syllabus`, or by hand (then usually without `hash`). Editing afterwards is normal and un-approves nothing; `classkit status` uses the hash to say 'edited since'. Agents never write or change it.

hash.description: sha256 of the syllabus at approval, without this block — front matter and body, comments aside (spec §8.9). Written by the tool; absent when approved by hand.
